turn_text: You did indeed. A lot has changed obviously in agriculture over the last 40 years as well. What about the way agriculture is developing? Do you think is positive and are you encouraged to see and what worries you after your years of service in these in these policy issues about the direction we're headed?

I'm very proud of the bio bills that we passed in terms of biotechnology. A couple of years back and we're still working on that. We just had a hearing on agriculture research and where we headed. down the road, everything, not everything, but pretty much everything depends on ag research. And show me a producer that does not have access to the current technology or research. And that cowboys are going to be in a lot of trouble. And the key along with broadband is to make this available to everybody out in farm country so they can at least compete. And we're doing amazing things in agriculture, just amazing things. Not too many people are really aware of that. That's something that we try to trumpet all the time on the Senate committee. But it's the classic thing that We're all in the same church and the same church pew, but the rest of the people aren't singing the same song, I guess. So we always have that problem to consider. Now, what am I worried about? Well, I look at the Obama Biden years. And I look at all the damn full regulations, pardon my language, rural fugitive dust, wildest, endangered species, a lesser prairie chicken. All of a sudden took off from Western Kansas because we didn't have enough rain. Then we got rain and guess what? The lesser prairie chicken came back. In the meantime, all the regs were coming out from EPA saying what you could do and what you couldn't do in that area because of that damn bird. If it rains, the lesser prairie chicken becomes the greater prairie chicken. And I just, it's crazy stuff, but all those regulations combined. I could list you 10 more. I'm afraid you're coming back because the same people that put them in are the same people now being nominated to be the assistant secretary or whoever it is that will be in charge of that. So I think we really have to guard against that and. So we've got some good people. We have to win Georgia. That's the biggest thing I've been telling agriculture. If you don't win Georgia, then you don't have John Bozeman as the chairman and he's going to make a great chairman. And of course he'll have a southern outlook, but he also is very much aware of what everybody's doing all over the country. So I'm worried about over regulation again, popping over the hill. I hope that doesn't take place. And I'll have something to say about it. I'll get my finger in the pie somehow.
